prompt_inputs.goal: Build muscle mass for competitive powerlifting

solution_criteria: Total daily calorie estimate exceeds maintenance level (surplus) appropriate for a 75kg athlete, roughly 3000-3500 kcal
Protein intake explicitly calculated or stated at approximately 1.6-2.2g per kg bodyweight (120-165g range)
Meal plan includes at least 4 distinct eating occasions (breakfast, lunch, dinner, plus snacks) with specific foods and portion sizes listed
Includes carbohydrate-rich foods timed around training to support strength performance
Plan is presented compactly (fits on roughly one page, no excessive filler text)

prompt_inputs.goal: Cut body fat while maintaining performance for marathon training

solution_criteria: All foods listed are strictly plant-based with no animal products (no dairy, eggs, honey, etc.)
No gluten-containing grains (wheat, barley, rye) appear anywhere in the plan; gluten-free alternatives like rice, quinoa, or oats (certified GF) are used instead
Calorie level reflects a moderate deficit while still supporting endurance training, roughly 1800-2200 kcal range with justification
Plant-based protein sources (e.g., lentils, tofu, tempeh, beans) are included in at least 3 meals to address vegan protein adequacy
Carbohydrate intake is sufficient to fuel marathon training (specific mention of pre/post-run fueling with GF carb sources)

prompt_inputs.goal: Simultaneously gain significant muscle mass and lose body fat quickly within 2 weeks
prompt_inputs.restrictions: Severe shellfish allergy and lactose intolerant, also trying to avoid all added sugar

solution_criteria: Response acknowledges the inherent tension/conflict in simultaneously bulking and cutting rapidly, and sets realistic expectations (e.g., body recomposition framing, or notes 2 weeks is too short for significant simultaneous gains) rather than ignoring the contradiction
No shellfish or shellfish-derived ingredients appear anywhere in the plan
No dairy-based lactose sources included (milk, regular cheese, ice cream) or lactose-free alternatives are explicitly specified if dairy is used
No added sugars appear in any meal or snack; natural sugars from whole fruit are acceptable but no syrups, sweetened sauces, or desserts with added sugar

Provides a specific, high-protein calorie target (e.g., protein around 2g/kg ~190g, calories set near maintenance or slight adjustment) with reasoning tied to the recomposition goal rather than an extreme deficit or surplus
